chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hajjal, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jamal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever performs the Hajj pilgrimage twice will remain in goodness until he dies.

key_terms.فِي خَيْرٍ: in goodness / in a state of blessing

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing the Hajj pilgrimage twice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to emphasize the cumulative spiritual elevation of the pilgrim, suggesting that the second Hajj builds upon the first to maintain a continuous state of divine grace (*khayr*) until death. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that Hajj is not merely a ritual obligation but a transformative journey that purifies the soul and sustains the believer's connection to God through repeated devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-81 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Al-Hijal, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Safvan ibn Mihran al-Jamal, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
Whoever goes on the Hajj pilgrimage twice would always be in good conditions until he dies.”
